review_target: server/migrations/004_access_control.up.sql (the SQL file itself), plus the verification harness (verify_004.sh, reapply_004.sh, scenario_b.sh) as evidence of what was actually checked. Cross-referenced against user-spec.md, tech-spec.md (Solution, Decision 3/4/5/10/11, Data Models), tasks/1.md, and existing migrations 002/003.
summary: The migration is a byte-for-byte copy of the tech-spec's Data Models SQL block (verified with diff) and of the task's own Details block — no drift between spec and delivery. I independently re-ran the implementer's own harness against a live MariaDB 11.4.12 container rather than trusting the claims: verify_004.sh (22/22 checks) passed against the project's live 'poshivon' DB, a hand re-apply of the raw file via reapply_004.sh completed with exit 0 and no duplicated schema objects, and scenario_b.sh — which builds the actual production-redeploy path (001-003 pre-recorded in schema_migrations, real pre-existing user rows, 004 applied alone by the real migrate.go/app binary) — passed all 5 backfill-specific assertions plus a second full idempotency pass. Every prior test-reviewer (design round 1) finding — full column-definition assertions instead of presence-only, CHECK clause text, FK join scoped to access_requests specifically, BINARY case-sensitive admin identity check, exit-code assertion on re-apply, and the scenario-B prod-redeploy path — has been implemented and is confirmed working live, not just claimed. I could not find a functional defect in the SQL. Naming (chk_*, fk_*_user, VARCHAR+CHECK over ENUM, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS) matches 002/003 exactly. Findings below are informational/minor observations a future maintainer should know about, not correctness bugs.

findings.description: users.id is VARCHAR(255) PRIMARY KEY with no explicit collation (inherited from 002_costing_schema.up.sql / DB default), and information_schema shows the default DB collation is case-insensitive (observed utf8mb4_uca1400_ai_ci on access_requests, created with no explicit COLLATE clause). That means a primary-key comparison on users.id is case-insensitive: 'RoGogDBD' and 'rogogdbd' collide as the same row. In practice this is benign for the seed INSERT itself (confirmed live: re-running the file does not create a second row under different casing, and EnsureUser's later ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE per Decision 11 only touches email/display_name, never role/has_access) — so a differently-cased login from Yandex would silently land on the same admin row rather than create a duplicate or a security gap. Flagging only because it is a non-obvious fact about this schema (case-insensitive PK matching on a column that is about to carry hardcoded, case-sensitive-looking real usernames) that the next person editing this file or debugging 'why didn't a third admin row appear' would want to know.
findings.recommendation: No code change needed for this task. Worth a one-line comment in the migration or in decisions.md noting that users.id matching is case-insensitive by default collation, so the two seeded logins are effectively case-insensitive keys despite being written in mixed case.

findings.description: ADD CONSTRAINT chk_users_role on the users table requires MariaDB to validate the CHECK against every existing row at ALTER time (unlike a plain ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT, which can often apply instantly). Because role is added with NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user' in the very same ALTER TABLE statement, every pre-existing row is already compliant by construction, so validation is fast today. This is a non-issue at current scale (confirmed via scenario_b.sh: the multi-clause ALTER TABLE on a non-empty users table completed well within the app's 10s startup grace period), but a future maintainer copying this migration's 'many ADD COLUMN + ADD CONSTRAINT in one ALTER' pattern onto a table with real production volume should know that adding a CHECK is not always as cheap as adding a column.
findings.recommendation: No action needed for this migration. Purely a note for future migrations that reuse this pattern against larger tables.

findings.description: Two real Yandex login usernames are now permanently in git history via a migration file that Decision 4 explicitly says must never be edited post-application (down-migrations don't exist, and a later fix would be a manual DB operation, not a re-run of this file). This is a deliberate, well-reasoned trade-off already argued through two rounds of tech-spec validation (commits b6fb0d9 'real admin logins', 6fd5bef 'CSRF... real admin logins') and isn't something to relitigate here — flagging only as a recorded fact for the record, since it's the kind of thing a future contributor skimming git blame on this file without the tech-spec context might be surprised by.
findings.recommendation: No action needed — already an accepted, documented decision. Not asking for a change.

strengths: Verbatim match to tech-spec Data Models and to the task's own Details block — verified with diff, not by inspection.

Genuinely idempotent: independently re-ran the raw file against a live DB twice and confirmed zero duplicated indexes/constraints/rows, not just an unchanged row count (which alone could mask a partial second-run failure — this is exactly what reapply_004.sh's exit-code + ERROR-grep check guards against).

The two-scenario Acceptance Criteria (clean DB vs. DB carrying prod schema 001+002+003) is genuinely exercised, not just nominally claimed: scenario_b.sh builds the real migrate.go version-skip path with a real pre-existing non-admin row and a real pre-existing admin-to-be row, and confirms the exact edge cases the tech-spec calls out (Decision 4's 'INSERT not UPDATE' rationale, Decision 10's 'has_access untouched on promotion' rationale) with live data, not just at the SQL-reading level.
Naming and style fully consistent with 002/003: chk_* / fk_*_user naming, VARCHAR+CHECK over ENUM (Decision 4's stated rationale), CREATE INDEX/ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS idioms already used in 003.

MariaDB 11.4 compatibility claims (ADD COLUMN/ADD CONSTRAINT/CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS) verified against a real mariadb:11.4.12 container in this review, not taken on faith from the tech-spec's claim.
verification_performed: Read the migration file, 002/003 for style baseline, migrate.go for apply semantics, and all three harness scripts. Then independently executed (not just read) verify_004.sh against the live poshivon DB (22/22 pass), reapply_004.sh (client exit 0, no ERROR output, state unchanged, 22/22 pass), and scenario_b.sh end-to-end (fresh poshivon_b DB, 001-003 applied and recorded manually, pre-existing legacy_user + RoGogDBD rows seeded, real poshivon-app container run to exercise migrate.go's actual version-skip + apply path, all schema/backfill/idempotency assertions passed). Confirmed MariaDB version live: 11.4.12-MariaDB-ubu2404. Confirmed migrations.Run() executes before the HTTP server starts serving (server/cmd/main.go:32-36), so no race between the seed INSERT and a concurrent EnsureUser call is possible.
